lesson.title: Full passage A: organised sport and education

learning_objectives.en: Read 9 paragraphs and identify what the study can and cannot establish.
learning_objectives.vi: Đọc 9 đoạn, phân biệt bằng chứng và kết luận có giới hạn.

content.en: Choose the main point that explains the whole text, not a detail from one paragraph.
content.vi: Chọn ý chính bao quát toàn bài, không chỉ một số liệu hoặc chi tiết ở một đoạn.

strategies.en: Skim 90 seconds to label paragraph roles; answer questions using exact evidence, then review option wording.
strategies.vi: Đọc lướt 90 giây để gắn nhãn các đoạn; tìm bằng chứng rồi kiểm tra cách diễn đạt của phương án.

mini_review.en: Can you name one confounding factor and one finding the authors support?
mini_review.vi: Bạn nêu được một yếu tố gây nhiễu và một phát hiện có bằng chứng?

passages.title: Does organised sport make better students?
passages.text:
[A] For decades, schools have defended after-school sport by claiming that it does more than keep children fit. Teams, coaches and weekly matches are said to teach discipline, cooperation and the ability to recover from failure – qualities that should also help in the classroom. Yet when education budgets are tight, sport is often among the first activities to be reduced, partly because its academic benefits are difficult to demonstrate.

[B] A five-year study carried out in the fictional region of Westmoor attempted to measure those benefits more carefully. Researchers followed 2,300 students aged eleven to sixteen in eighteen secondary schools. Around half took part in organised sport at least twice a week; the rest did not. Each year, the researchers collected exam results, attendance records and questionnaires about how students felt at school.

[C] At first sight, the results seemed to confirm the traditional view. Students who played organised sport had higher average exam scores and missed fewer days of school. However, the research team pointed out a serious difficulty. Families who pay for sports clubs, transport and equipment are, on average, better off than those who do not, and wealthier families also tend to provide more help with homework. The sport itself might therefore not be responsible for the better results.

[D] To address this problem, the researchers compared students from similar backgrounds, including pupils whose clubs were free because they were run by the school. Once family income was taken into account, the difference in exam scores became much smaller, though it did not disappear completely. The difference in attendance, on the other hand, remained clear. Students who belonged to a team were noticeably less likely to miss school, particularly on days when matches or training sessions took place.

[E] Interviews with students suggested why. Many said that their team was one of the main reasons they enjoyed school, and that they did not want to let teammates down. Coaches also reported that they often noticed when a student seemed unhappy or tired before teachers did, because they saw the same small group regularly in a relaxed setting. In the words of one coach, “Training is the only hour of the week when some of these kids feel they are good at something.”

[F] Not every finding was positive. A minority of students, most often those who played at a high competitive level, reported that training left them too tired to study in the evening, and their grades fell during the main competition season. The researchers concluded that the amount of sport mattered: two or three sessions a week appeared helpful, while daily training was linked with lower marks for some students.

[G] The researchers also looked at which sports seemed to matter most. Team games such as football, basketball and netball were linked with the largest improvement in attendance, while individual activities such as running and swimming showed a smaller effect. One explanation offered in the report is that team members notice when someone is missing and ask why, which gives students a reason to turn up even on days when they would rather stay at home.

[H] Teachers interviewed for the study were divided about what schools should do with these findings. Some argued that the benefits were too small to justify the cost of transport, equipment and staff time, especially when examination results are what parents and inspectors look at first. Others replied that a student who attends regularly has more chances to learn, so a small effect on attendance could add up to a meaningful difference over five years of secondary school.

[I] The study’s authors are careful about what their evidence shows. They argue that organised sport is unlikely to raise exam scores dramatically on its own, but that it may keep some students connected to school who might otherwise drift away. In my view, that alone is a strong reason for schools to protect free sports clubs, especially in areas where families cannot afford private ones.

exercises.title: Reading passage A – critical multiple choice

instruction.en: Read passage R-A, choose ONE answer for each question.
instruction.vi: Đọc bài R-A và chọn MỘT đáp án.

questions.prompt_en: What was the research group trying to understand?
questions.prompt_vi: Nhóm nghiên cứu muốn tìm hiểu điều gì?
options: The effects associated with organised sport
How to build a new sports centre

accepted: The effects associated with organised sport

questions.explanation_en: Paragraph B explains that the study measured links between sport, exams and attendance.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn B nói nghiên cứu mối liên hệ giữa thể thao, kết quả thi và chuyên cần.

questions.prompt_vi: Có bao nhiêu học sinh được theo dõi?
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph B gives the exact sample as 2,300 students.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn B nêu rõ cỡ mẫu 2.300.

questions.prompt_en: Why were the first results difficult to interpret?
questions.prompt_vi: Tại sao kết quả ban đầu khó diễn giải?
options: The study had no school attendance data
Family wealth might influence both activities and scores
The researchers studied only one student

accepted: Family wealth might influence both activities and scores

questions.explanation_en: Paragraph C introduces household income as a confounding influence.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn C nêu điều kiện gia đình là yếu tố gây nhiễu.

questions.prompt_en: What happened after income differences were taken into account?
questions.prompt_vi: Điều gì xảy ra khi xét điều kiện thu nhập?
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph D: the exam-score gap decreased but did not disappear.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn D: chênh lệch điểm thu hẹp nhưng vẫn còn.

questions.prompt_vi: Kết quả nào vẫn khác biệt rõ?
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph D states attendance differences remained clear.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn D nói khác biệt về chuyên cần vẫn rõ.

questions.prompt_en: Why did some students want to attend school?
questions.prompt_vi: Tại sao một số học sinh muốn đến trường?
options: They did not want to let teammates down

accepted: They did not want to let teammates down

questions.explanation_en: Paragraph E links team loyalty to attendance.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn E liên hệ trách nhiệm với đồng đội và việc đến trường.

questions.prompt_en: What was a risk of very frequent competition?
questions.prompt_vi: Rủi ro khi thi đấu với tần suất dày?
options: Tiredness and falling grades for some students

accepted: Tiredness and falling grades for some students

questions.explanation_en: Paragraph F describes tiredness and lower marks for a minority.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn F đề cập một số học sinh mệt và giảm điểm.

questions.prompt_en: Which activities showed a stronger attendance link?
questions.prompt_vi: Hoạt động nào liên hệ mạnh hơn với chuyên cần?
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph G compares team games with individual activities.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn G so sánh môn đồng đội với môn cá nhân.

questions.prompt_vi: Người phản đối chú trọng điều gì?
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph H discusses the cost and emphasis on exam results.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn H nói về chi phí và ưu tiên kết quả thi.

questions.prompt_en: Which statement best summarises the study?
questions.prompt_vi: Tóm tắt nào phù hợp nhất?
options: Sport may support attendance, not transform grades by itself

accepted: Sport may support attendance, not transform grades by itself

questions.explanation_en: Paragraph I limits the claim and focuses on school engagement.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn I nêu giới hạn kết luận và vai trò gắn kết với trường.

questions.prompt_en: What kind of qualification is needed to interpret the findings?
questions.prompt_vi: Điều kiện nào cần để diễn giải nghiên cứu đúng?
questions.explanation_en: Paragraphs C–D warn that an observed link is not automatically causal.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn C–D lưu ý tương quan không đồng nghĩa quan hệ nhân quả.

questions.prompt_en: What is the writer’s own stated position?
questions.prompt_vi: Quan điểm cá nhân của tác giả?
options: Private clubs should replace school clubs
questions.explanation_en: The final sentence says “In my view…” and supports free clubs.
questions.explanation_vi: Câu kết với “In my view…” ủng hộ bảo vệ câu lạc bộ miễn phí.

instruction.en: Select the statement supported by the passage.
instruction.vi: Chọn mệnh đề được bài đọc xác nhận.

questions.prompt_en: Which claim is a cautious interpretation rather than a proven cause?
questions.prompt_vi: Kết luận nào là diễn giải thận trọng, không phải nguyên nhân đã chứng minh?
options: Organised sport causes every student to get better marks
Organised sport may keep students connected to school
Coaches replace teachers for every child

accepted: Organised sport may keep students connected to school

questions.explanation_en: The authors avoid claiming certain causal gains in exam scores.
questions.explanation_vi: Tác giả không khẳng định chắc chắn thể thao làm tăng điểm.

questions.prompt_en: What made free school clubs useful for comparison?
questions.prompt_vi: Vì sao câu lạc bộ miễn phí có ích cho đối chiếu?
options: They were the only clubs with top athletes
They reduced the effect of family ability to pay
They removed the need for all examinations

accepted: They reduced the effect of family ability to pay

questions.explanation_en: Paragraph D compares pupils from similar backgrounds and free clubs.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn D so sánh học sinh cùng nền tảng và câu lạc bộ miễn phí.
